intent.raw_query: Tokyo city break, $3000 for couple, food and tech culture, April 2026 from SFO

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the famous Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street food from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food stall owners to learn about Tokyo's culinary heritage and the art of Japanese breakfast culture.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech & Anime District Exploration
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's legendary electronics and tech culture hub. Visit multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, explore retro gaming arcades, maid cafes, and cutting-edge gadget shops that define Japan's unique intersection of technology and pop culture.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in a world-renowned digital art experience created by the art collective teamLab. Walk through stunning interactive installations that blend technology, nature, and art in a borderless, ever-changing environment — a perfect fusion of tech culture and artistic expression.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, and stroll through the historic Nakamise shopping street. Experience traditional ceremonies, purchase handcrafted souvenirs, and explore the preserved Edo-period atmosphere of Asakusa, one of Tokyo's most culturally rich neighborhoods.

experiences.name: Ramen Tasting Tour in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided or guided ramen crawl through Shinjuku's famous Ramen Street and surrounding alleyways. Sample regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso from legendary local ramen shops, and discover the craft and passion behind Japan's most beloved comfort food.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Tokyo, Japan
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities — flight arrives at 22:30
day_by_day.afternoon: No activities — in transit
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30 on flight UA. Clear customs and immigration, collect luggage, and purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for convenient train travel throughout your stay. Take the airport limousine bus or Narita Express (N'EX) to your hotel area. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort, Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane or at airport
meals.dinner: Grab a quick bite at a 24-hour convenience store (7-Eleven, Lawson, or FamilyMart) near the hotel — onigiri rice balls, sandwiches, and hot foods available for under ¥600

day_by_day.notes: Given the late arrival, keep Day 1 simple. Convenience stores (conbini) in Japan are excellent and affordable — perfect for a late-night meal. Confirm hotel check-in arrangements in advance since arrival is after 10 PM. Exchange some yen at the airport for small cash needs.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recover from jet lag. After a slow start, head to the nearby neighborhood to explore on foot. Visit a local shotengai (shopping street) to get a feel for everyday Tokyo life. Pick up breakfast at a local bakery or convenience store.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train to Akihabara — Tokyo's famous Electric Town and tech culture hub. Explore multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera and Sofmap. Browse retro game shops, anime merchandise stores, and gadget stalls. Many items are free to browse and the sensory experience is priceless.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through Akihabara's neon-lit streets after dark for a stunning visual experience. Visit a maid café for a unique cultural experience (budget around ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a drink and entry). Head back to the hotel early to rest and fully adjust to the time zone.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store or local bakery — onigiri, tamagoyaki, coffee (under ¥500)
meals.lunch: Akihabara ramen shop — try a bowl of shoyu or tonkotsu ramen for ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Yoshinoya or Matsuya gyudon (beef bowl) chain near Akihabara station — filling and budget-friendly at ¥500–¥700

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is easily accessible by JR Yamanote Line. Most electronics stores open around 10–11 AM. Free Wi-Fi is available throughout the area. April weather in Tokyo is typically mild (15–20°C) with possible cherry blossoms still in bloom — bring a light jacket.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Asakusa, one of Tokyo's most traditional districts. Visit Senso-ji Temple — Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple. Walk through Nakamise-dori shopping street lined with traditional snack vendors and souvenir shops. Arrive early (before 9 AM) to beat crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center (free) for panoramic views of Senso-ji from above. Walk along the Sumida River and enjoy the spring scenery. Cross over to Ueno Park (15-minute walk or short train ride) and explore the park grounds, which may still have late cherry blossoms in mid-April.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Ameyoko Market in Ueno — a vibrant outdoor market with street food, fresh produce, and cheap goods. Try yakitori skewers, takoyaki (octopus balls), and fresh fruit. Browse stalls for affordable snacks and local goods.

meals.breakfast: Grab ningyo-yaki (small cakes filled with red bean paste) from a Nakamise-dori vendor in Asakusa for ¥200–¥400
meals.lunch: Asakusa soba restaurant — try zaru soba (cold buckwheat noodles) for ¥700–¥1,000
meals.dinner: Ameyoko Market street food — mix of takoyaki (¥400), yakitori skewers (¥150–¥200 each), and fresh seafood snacks; budget ¥800–¥1,200 total

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, though the inner hall has specific hours. Ueno Park is free. Ameyoko Market is liveliest in the late afternoon and early evening. Wear comfortable walking shoes — this is a full walking day.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Shibuya — start with the world-famous Shibuya Crossing scramble intersection. Watch the organized chaos from street level, then head up to the free observation area at Mag's Park (Shibuya Hikarie or Shibuya Stream rooftop for views). Explore the surrounding streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk uphill to Harajuku and stroll down Takeshita Street — a colorful, youth fashion street packed with quirky shops, crepe stands, and pop culture. Browse the free-to-enter boutiques and soak in the unique street culture. Then walk through Omotesando for a contrast of upscale architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Shibuya for dinner and evening atmosphere. Visit Don Quijote (Donki) — a famous discount variety store open late — for budget shopping and entertainment. Great place to pick up snacks, cosmetics, and unique Japanese products.

meals.breakfast: Doutor Coffee shop near Shibuya station — morning set (toast, egg, coffee) for ¥500–¥600
meals.lunch: Harajuku crepe from Marion Crêpes or a street vendor on Takeshita Street — ¥500–¥700
meals.dinner: Shibuya Ichiran Ramen — individual booth ramen dining experience, tonkotsu ramen for ¥980–¥1,200

day_by_day.notes: Harajuku and Shibuya are connected by a short walk or one train stop on the Yamanote Line. Takeshita Street is most vibrant on weekday afternoons. If visiting on a weekend, expect larger crowds. The Meiji Shrine is a 5-minute walk from Harajuku station and is free to enter — consider adding a quick visit.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku — start with a visit to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building (free observation deck on the 45th floor) for panoramic 360-degree views of the city and potentially Mt. Fuji on a clear day. Open from 9 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (entry ¥500) — one of Tokyo's most beautiful parks, especially lovely in April with late cherry blossoms or spring flowers. Spend 2–3 hours relaxing and picnicking in the garden.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the electric nightlife of Kabukicho — Shinjuku's famous entertainment district. Walk through Golden Gai (a maze of tiny atmospheric bars) and Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) — a narrow alley of small yakitori restaurants with smoky, nostalgic charm. Have dinner at one of the tiny yakitori stalls.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel or a standing soba shop near Shinjuku station — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Picnic in Shinjuku Gyoen — grab bento boxes and snacks from a nearby convenience store or supermarket basement food hall (depachika) for ¥600–¥900
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho yakitori dinner — skewers of chicken, vegetables, and offal grilled over charcoal; budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 including a beer or soft drink

day_by_day.notes: Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck is free but closed on select Mondays and Tuesdays — check the schedule in advance. Shinjuku Gyoen does not allow alcohol. Omoide Yokocho restaurants are tiny (4–8 seats each) — be prepared to share space with strangers, which adds to the charm.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Odaiba — Tokyo's futuristic waterfront island accessible via the scenic Yurikamome monorail (Suica card accepted). Visit teamLab Borderless or teamLab Planets (book tickets online in advance — ¥3,200). This is a world-renowned digital art museum and a must for tech and culture lovers.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore the rest of Odaiba for free. Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza to see the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue outside (free). Browse the Aqua City and DiverCity malls for window shopping. Enjoy views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline from the waterfront promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to the mainland and visit Toyosu Market (if interested in fresh seafood) or return to your neighborhood for a relaxed evening. Visit a local izakaya (Japanese pub) for affordable drinks and small plates.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area café or convenience store — ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court in Aqua City or DiverCity — ramen, curry, or sushi sets for ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Local neighborhood izakaya — order draft beer (nama biru) and share plates of edamame, karaage (fried chicken), and grilled fish; budget ¥1,500–¥2,000 per person

day_by_day.notes: Book teamLab tickets online well in advance as they often sell out. The Yurikamome monorail offers stunning views of the bay — sit at the front for the best experience. Odaiba is very walkable once you arrive. Consider visiting on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanaka — one of Tokyo's most preserved old-town neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander through Yanaka Cemetery (free, beautiful in spring with tree-lined paths), browse the historic Yanaka Ginza shopping street, and discover traditional craft shops, old temples, and local bakeries.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to nearby Nezu Shrine — a lesser-known but stunning shrine with hundreds of torii gates (similar to Kyoto's Fushimi Inari but far less crowded and free to enter). Then explore Nezu and Sendagi neighborhoods on foot — charming, quiet, and very local.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji or Shimokitazawa — two bohemian neighborhoods beloved by young Tokyoites for their vintage shops, live music venues, and independent cafés. Browse second-hand clothing stores and enjoy the alternative local culture.

meals.breakfast: Local bakery in Yanaka Ginza — fresh-baked melon pan or cream puffs for ¥150–¥300
meals.lunch: Yanaka Ginza street food — menchi katsu (fried meat cutlet) croquette for ¥150–¥200, plus other snacks; budget ¥500–¥800
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa curry restaurant — Japanese-style curry is a local staple and very affordable at ¥800–¥1,100

day_by_day.notes: Yanaka is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The neighborhood has a nostalgic, slow-paced atmosphere very different from central Tokyo. Nezu Shrine's torii gate tunnel is most photogenic in the morning light. Shimokitazawa is about 30 minutes by train from Yanaka via transfer.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Tsukiji Outer Market (the inner wholesale market moved to Toyosu, but the outer market remains active and free to explore). Browse fresh seafood stalls, sushi restaurants, and specialty food shops. Enjoy a fresh sushi breakfast — one of Tokyo's most iconic food experiences.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short train ride to Ginza — Tokyo's upscale shopping and arts district. Browse the free galleries inside department stores (Matsuya, Mitsukoshi) and visit the free Itchome Ginza gallery spaces. Window shop along Chuo-dori. Visit the Apple Store Tokyo or Sony Park for free tech culture immersion.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Nihonbashi or Marunouchi for a walk along the historic bridge and riverside. Visit the Coredo Muromachi complex for evening atmosphere. Return to the hotel or explore a local neighborhood izakaya.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh sushi set (maguro, salmon, uni if budget allows) from a market stall for ¥1,000–¥1,500; arrive by 8–9 AM for freshest selection
meals.lunch: Ginza basement food hall (depachika) bento box or standing sushi bar — ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Nearby ramen or gyoza restaurant — gyoza set with rice and soup for ¥700–¥900

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest and freshest early morning (7–10 AM). Many stalls close by early afternoon. Ginza can feel intimidating due to luxury brands, but most galleries, department store food halls, and public spaces are completely free to enter and enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours from Tokyo by Tobu Nikko Line — budget option around ¥1,400 one way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine complex — ornate, colorful shrines and mausoleums set in a cedar forest. Entry to the main complex is ¥1,300.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko — visit Rinnoji Temple, Futarasan Shrine (included in combo ticket), and walk the forested paths. If time permits, take a bus to Kegon Falls — one of Japan's most spectacular waterfalls (elevator to viewing platform ¥570).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening. Grab dinner near your home station and rest after a full day of travel and exploration.

meals.breakfast: Convenience store near hotel before departing — onigiri and coffee for ¥400–¥500
meals.lunch: Nikko yuba (tofu skin) cuisine — a local specialty; try a yuba soba or yuba donburi set at a local restaurant for ¥900–¥1,300
meals.dinner: Neighborhood ramen or udon shop near hotel — ¥700–¥1,000

day_by_day.notes: Purchase the Tobu Nikko All Area Pass for best value if planning to use local buses in Nikko (¥4,780 from Asakusa). Alternatively, use the regular Tobu Nikko Line for just the train. Nikko can be very crowded on weekends — a weekday visit is recommended. Wear comfortable shoes for uneven stone paths.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Kagurazaka — a charming Franco-Japanese neighborhood in central Tokyo. Explore the narrow cobblestone alleyways (yokocho), traditional ryotei restaurants, and French bakeries. Visit Akagi Shrine — a beautifully modern redesigned shrine by architect Kengo Kuma (free entry).
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Jimbocho — Tokyo's famous used bookstore district. Browse thousands of secondhand books, vintage maps, manga, and academic texts. Even without buying, the district is a fascinating cultural experience for book and knowledge lovers. Nearby, visit the free Printing Museum or browse Ochanomizu's music instrument shops.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Akihabara again in the evening for a different atmosphere — explore multi-story arcades (game centers), try crane games, and experience the gaming culture. Many arcades are open until midnight.

meals.breakfast: Kagurazaka French bakery — croissant and café au lait for ¥500–¥700
meals.lunch: Jimbocho curry — the neighborhood is famous for its curry restaurants; try a katsu curry set for ¥900–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Akihabara standing sushi bar or conveyor belt sushi (kaiten-zushi) — budget ¥1,000–¥1,500 for a satisfying meal

day_by_day.notes: Kagurazaka is best explored on foot — the hidden alleys (kakuriyo) are easy to miss but worth seeking out. Jimbocho bookstores are mostly open 10 AM–7 PM. Akihabara game centers are open until late — bring ¥1,000–¥2,000 in coins for arcade games if interested.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the Nakameguro area — walk along the Meguro River canal, lined with cherry trees (may have late blossoms or fresh green leaves in late April). Browse the trendy boutiques, cafés, and concept stores along the riverside. This is one of Tokyo's most photogenic neighborhoods.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short train ride to Daikanyama and Ebisu — upscale but walkable neighborhoods with free-to-browse architecture, galleries, and the iconic Daikanyama T-Site (Tsutaya Books) — a stunning bookstore and cultural complex worth visiting even without buying.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Roppongi for Tokyo's art and nightlife district. Visit the free outdoor art installations around Roppongi Hills or 21_21 Design Sight (exterior viewing is free). If budget allows, visit Mori Art Museum (¥2,000) for contemporary art with panoramic city views.

meals.breakfast: Nakameguro café — avocado toast or Japanese breakfast set for ¥600–¥900
meals.lunch: Ebisu depachika (department store basement food hall) — grab a variety of prepared foods and eat in a nearby park; budget ¥800–¥1,200
meals.dinner: Roppongi area — try a standing yakitori bar or ramen shop for ¥800–¥1,200; avoid sit-down restaurants in Roppongi as prices skew high for tourists

day_by_day.notes: Nakameguro is most beautiful in cherry blossom season (late March–early April) but remains charming in late April. Daikanyama T-Site is free to browse and a must-visit for design and culture enthusiasts. Roppongi can be expensive — stick to ramen and standing bars for budget dining.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Planets or explore the National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation (Miraikan) in Odaiba (entry ¥630) — a world-class science and technology museum covering robotics, AI, space exploration, and the internet. Perfect for tech culture enthusiasts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to central Tokyo and visit Hamarikyu Gardens (entry ¥300) — a beautiful traditional Japanese garden with a teahouse on the water, set against the backdrop of modern skyscrapers. Take a water bus from Hamarikyu to Asakusa along the Sumida River (¥1,020) for a scenic river cruise.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Asakusa — revisit Senso-ji at night when it's beautifully illuminated and less crowded. Browse the 24-hour Nakamise-dori for last-minute souvenir shopping. Enjoy a farewell dinner in the neighborhood.

meals.breakfast: Hotel area or convenience store — ¥400–¥500
meals.lunch: Odaiba food court or Miraikan café — ramen or curry for ¥800–¥1,100
meals.dinner: Asakusa tempura restaurant — try tendon (tempura over rice) at Daikokuya or a similar local spot for ¥1,200–¥1,800; a Tokyo classic

day_by_day.notes: Miraikan is closed on Tuesdays — plan accordingly. The Sumida River water bus is a scenic and relaxing way to travel between Odaiba/Hamarikyu and Asakusa — highly recommended over the train for this leg. Book water bus tickets at the pier. Senso-ji at night is magical and far less crowded than daytime.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the final morning doing any last-minute exploration near the hotel. Visit a local supermarket or convenience store to stock up on Japanese snacks, instant ramen, and unique food items to bring home as affordable gifts. Pack bags and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on flight time, use remaining hours wisely. If time allows, revisit a favorite neighborhood or grab one last bowl of ramen at a local shop. Head to the airport with plenty of time — allow 2–3 hours before departure for check-in and security. Use your Suica card for the airport train.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Tokyo — check Suica card balance and either use remaining balance at airport shops or refund it at a JR machine (refund available minus a ¥220 handling fee). Reflect on 13 incredible days in one of the world's greatest cities.

meals.breakfast: Local café or convenience store near hotel — final Japanese breakfast of onigiri, miso soup, and green tea for ¥400–¥600
meals.lunch: Airport ramen or sushi restaurant at Narita/Haneda — slightly pricier than city but still reasonable at ¥1,000–¥1,500; a great final meal
meals.dinner: On the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for airport transfer — Narita is 60–90 minutes from central Tokyo, Haneda is 30–45 minutes. Confirm your terminal and airline check-in requirements. Most Japanese airports have excellent duty-free shops and food options. Use any remaining yen on airport food, snacks, or duty-free — it's difficult to exchange coins back to foreign currency.

trip_options.title: Classic Tokyo, Japan Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: N/A – In transit. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: N/A – In transit.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30. Clear immigration and customs, collect luggage, and take the airport limousine bus or Narita Express to central Tokyo. Check in to Aegean Bliss Resort. Unwind with a convenience store snack run – Tokyo's 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, and Lawson are legendary for quality onigiri, sandwiches, and hot foods available 24/7.

meals.breakfast: On the plane
meals.lunch: On the plane
meals.dinner: Convenience store (conbini) near hotel – try onigiri, karaage chicken, and a hot canned coffee for an authentic late-night Tokyo experience (~¥800–¥1,200)

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some yen at the airport currency counter or use a 7-Bank ATM (widely accepts foreign cards). Purchase a Suica or Pasmo IC card at the airport for seamless train and bus travel throughout the trip. Keep Day 1 light – jet lag will be significant.

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in to recover from jet lag. After a slow start, head to the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive by 9:00–10:00 AM to explore the bustling stalls. Sample fresh sushi, tamagoyaki (rolled egg omelette), grilled scallops, and seasonal street snacks from local vendors. The market is a living museum of Tokyo's culinary soul.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Hamarikyu Gardens (¥300 entry), a stunning traditional Japanese garden with a tidal pond, teahouse, and seasonal cherry blossom or spring flora. Enjoy matcha tea at the garden's historic Nakajima no Ochaya teahouse overlooking the water.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ginza for an evening stroll. Window-shop the iconic boulevard and explore the Itoya stationery flagship store. Dine at a mid-range sushi restaurant in the area for a proper sit-down sushi experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or nearby café – try a Japanese morning set (tamago gohan, miso soup, grilled fish) at a local kissaten (coffee shop)
meals.lunch: Tsukiji Outer Market – graze on fresh tuna sushi, tamagoyaki skewers, and fresh oysters from multiple stalls (~¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.dinner: Sushi Zanmai or Kyubey in Ginza – mid-range sushi restaurant offering omakase or à la carte sets (~¥3,000–¥6,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is busiest in the morning. Arrive early for the freshest products. Wear comfortable shoes – lots of walking. The Hamarikyu Gardens offer beautiful spring scenery in April.

day_by_day.morning: Full day in Akihabara – Tokyo's legendary tech and anime district. Start your Akihabara Tech & Anime District Exploration at 10:00 AM when stores open. Visit Yodobashi Camera (massive multi-floor electronics megastore), explore retro game shops like Super Potato, and browse the latest gadgets at Sofmap and BIC Camera.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Akihabara. Visit a maid café for a uniquely Tokyo cultural experience (budget ~¥1,500–¥2,000 for a drink and performance). Explore Kotobukiya for collectible figures and Animate for manga and anime merchandise. Check out the Radio Kaikan building for vintage electronics and rare tech components.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Akihabara or walk to nearby Kanda for dinner. Explore the vibrant evening atmosphere as neon signs light up the district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a nearby bakery/café
meals.lunch: Akihabara – try a themed restaurant or grab a bento from a department store basement food hall (depachika). Recommended: AKB48 Café or a curry house (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Kanda Yabu Soba – a historic soba restaurant near Akihabara serving handmade buckwheat noodles in a traditional setting (~¥1,500–¥2,500). Alternatively, try a ramen shop in the area.

day_by_day.notes: Most Akihabara stores open at 10:00–11:00 AM and close around 20:00–21:00. Carry cash as some smaller shops may not accept cards. The district is especially atmospheric after dark with its neon lighting.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk. Arrive early (8:00–9:00 AM) to experience the temple before crowds build. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon (Thunder Gate) and Nakamise-dori shopping street lined with traditional crafts, snacks, and souvenirs. Explore the temple grounds, the five-story pagoda, and the surrounding Asakusa neighborhood.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Yanaka neighborhood – one of Tokyo's best-preserved old shitamachi (downtown) areas. Stroll through Yanaka Ginza shopping street, browse independent shops, and visit the peaceful Yanaka Cemetery, which is particularly beautiful in April with cherry blossoms. Explore local galleries and artisan studios.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Ueno for the evening. Visit Ameya-Yokocho (Ameyoko) market for street food and lively shopping atmosphere. Enjoy dinner in Ueno.

meals.breakfast: Asakusa – try ningyo-yaki (small sponge cakes filled with red bean paste) and fresh-baked melon pan from Nakamise-dori stalls (~¥500–¥800)
meals.lunch: Yanaka – Kayaba Coffee, a beautifully restored 1938 café serving egg sandwiches and coffee in a nostalgic atmosphere (~¥1,200–¥1,800)
meals.dinner: Ueno – Ippudo Ramen or a local izakaya (Japanese gastropub) near Ameyoko market for yakitori, edamame, and cold Asahi beer (~¥2,000–¥3,500)

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is free to enter and open 24 hours, though the Nakamise shops open around 10:00 AM. Saturday will be busy – arrive early. Yanaka is a wonderful contrast to tourist-heavy Asakusa and feels like stepping back in time.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Harajuku and Meiji Jingu Shrine. Start with the serene forested walk to Meiji Jingu, Tokyo's most important Shinto shrine dedicated to Emperor Meiji. The forested path is peaceful and beautiful in spring. Then walk to Harajuku's Takeshita-dori street for Tokyo's wildest fashion subcultures and crepe shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk through Omotesando – Tokyo's 'Champs-Élysées' – lined with flagship stores from Japanese and international designers. Explore the Omotesando Hills complex (designed by Tadao Ando) and browse boutiques. Head to nearby Shibuya to witness the famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing, the world's busiest pedestrian intersection.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Shibuya's vibrant evening scene. Visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck (¥2,000) for panoramic night views of the city, including the iconic crossing from above.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Harajuku – Marion Crêpes (a Harajuku institution since 1976) for a sweet crepe, followed by a sit-down lunch at a café on Omotesando (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: Shibuya – Ichiran Ramen (solo dining booths, tonkotsu ramen) or Gyukatsu Motomura for crispy beef cutlet sets (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Meiji Jingu is free to enter. Sunday morning is a great time to see cosplayers in Harajuku near the bridge by Yoyogi Park. The Shibuya Sky observation deck requires advance online booking – book at least a day ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum. Book tickets in advance online (¥3,200 per person). Arrive at opening time (10:00 AM) to experience the immersive, boundary-free digital art installations before crowds arrive. The museum features interconnected rooms where art flows between spaces – allow 2–3 hours minimum.
day_by_day.afternoon: After teamLab, explore the Odaiba waterfront area. Visit DiverCity Tokyo Plaza to see the life-size Unicorn Gundam statue (free). Browse the futuristic Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) for robotics, AI, and space exhibits (¥630 entry).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the Odaiba waterfront at sunset with views of Rainbow Bridge and the Tokyo skyline. Dine at Aqua City Odaiba shopping mall which has a wide range of mid-range restaurants with bay views.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a café near the hotel
meals.lunch: teamLab Borderless café inside the museum or nearby DiverCity food court (~¥1,200–¥2,000)
meals.dinner: Aqua City Odaiba – Bills (Australian-Japanese fusion with bay views) or a Japanese barbecue (yakiniku) restaurant (~¥2,500–¥4,000)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless tickets MUST be booked online in advance – they frequently sell out weeks ahead. Wear comfortable clothing without high heels as you'll be walking through darkened rooms. The Miraikan is excellent for tech enthusiasts and has an English audio guide.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko (approximately 2 hours by Tobu Nikko Line from Asakusa, ~¥1,400 each way). Visit the UNESCO World Heritage Tosho-gu Shrine, an ornate mausoleum dedicated to Tokugawa Ieyasu featuring intricate carvings including the famous 'See no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil' monkeys. Explore the surrounding cedar forest.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Nikko – visit Rinno-ji Temple, the Yomeimon Gate (Gate of Sunlight), and stroll along the cedar-lined Omotesando avenue. In spring, the area is beautiful with cherry blossoms and fresh greenery.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by early evening (aim to depart Nikko by 16:00). Arrive back in Tokyo by 18:30. Enjoy a relaxed dinner near the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departing
meals.lunch: Nikko – Gyoshintei restaurant near the shrines for traditional shojin ryori (Buddhist vegetarian cuisine) in a historic setting (~¥2,500–¥4,000), or a bento from a local shop
meals.dinner: Near hotel – a neighborhood ramen shop or izakaya for a casual, restorative meal after a day of sightseeing (~¥1,500–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: Nikko Tosho-gu entry is ¥1,300. Purchase a combined pass for multiple temples/shrines. Start early – depart by 7:30–8:00 AM from Asakusa for a full day. The Tobu Nikko Line is the most economical option; consider the Nikko All Area Pass (¥4,780) which covers trains and buses.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Shinjuku. Start with a visit to the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building observation deck (free, opens 9:30 AM) for sweeping views of the city and, on clear days, Mount Fuji. Then explore the tranquil Shinjuku Gyoen National Garden (¥500 entry) – one of Japan's finest parks, especially beautiful in late cherry blossom season in April.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Shinjuku's diverse neighborhoods: visit the Golden Gai area (a network of tiny alleys with over 200 micro-bars), the Kabukicho entertainment district, and Takashimaya Times Square for depachika (basement food hall) browsing. Visit Isetan department store for premium Japanese food souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Experience Omoide Yokocho (Memory Lane) – a narrow alley of tiny yakitori stalls dating back to the post-WWII era. Sit at a counter, order skewers of grilled chicken and vegetables, and enjoy cold beer in this atmospheric, smoky, utterly authentic Tokyo setting.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Shinjuku Gyoen park – bring a picnic from a nearby konbini or depachika and dine among the gardens (~¥800–¥1,500)
meals.dinner: Omoide Yokocho (Piss Alley) – yakitori skewers, cold Sapporo draft beer, and grilled offal at tiny counter seats (~¥2,000–¥3,500 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Shinjuku Gyoen is a 'no alcohol' zone – save the beer for Omoide Yokocho. The Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building has both a north and south observation tower; the north tower offers slightly better views. Golden Gai bars are tiny (some seat only 5–6 people) and welcoming to tourists – look for signs saying 'tourists welcome.'

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Edo-Tokyo Museum (¥600 entry) in Ryogoku for an immersive journey through Tokyo's history from the Edo period to the modern era. The museum features full-scale reconstructions of Edo-era streets, bridges, and buildings. Excellent for understanding the cultural roots of modern Tokyo.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Ryogoku sumo district. Visit the Kokugikan Sumo Arena and its free sumo museum. Walk through the neighborhood to spot sumo stables (heya) and chanko nabe restaurants – the high-calorie hot pot eaten by sumo wrestlers. If visiting during a tournament (check schedule), tickets can be purchased from ¥3,800.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Koenji or Shimokitazawa for Tokyo's indie and alternative culture scene. Browse vintage clothing stores, independent record shops, and small live music venues. These neighborhoods represent a different, bohemian side of Tokyo culture.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or a local café
meals.lunch: Ryogoku – Chanko Tomoegata, a sumo stable-run chanko nabe restaurant near the Kokugikan serving the traditional wrestler's hot pot (~¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.dinner: Shimokitazawa – a local curry restaurant (the neighborhood is famous for curry houses) or a cozy izakaya (~¥2,000–¥3,000)

day_by_day.notes: Check the Japan Sumo Association website for tournament dates – the Tokyo basho (tournament) is typically held in January, May, and September. April may not have a tournament, but the museum and neighborhood are worth visiting regardless. Shimokitazawa is about 30 minutes from Ryogoku by train.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Yanesen area more deeply – visit the Tokyo National Museum in Ueno Park (¥1,000 entry), home to the world's largest collection of Japanese art and artifacts. Highlights include samurai armor, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculptures, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stroll through Ueno Park and visit Ueno Zoo (¥600) if interested, or relax in the park. Then head to Akihabara for any last electronics or tech shopping. Alternatively, visit the 2k540 AKI-OKA ARTISAN craft market under the train tracks between Akihabara and Okachimachi for handmade Japanese crafts and design goods.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Kanda-Jimbocho neighborhood – Tokyo's famous used bookstore and antiquarian district. Browse hundreds of shops selling old maps, vintage manga, rare books, and ukiyo-e prints. Many shops stay open until 20:00.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast
meals.lunch: Ueno – Ueno Seiyoken, a historic Western-style restaurant in Ueno Park serving yoshoku (Japanese-Western fusion) dishes like omurice and beef stew since 1876 (~¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.dinner: Jimbocho – Bondy, a legendary Japanese curry restaurant in the bookseller district, famous for their European-style curry served with cheese and boiled eggs (~¥1,800–¥2,500)

day_by_day.notes: The Tokyo National Museum is closed on Mondays. The 2k540 craft market is closed on Wednesdays and Thursdays. Jimbocho is best explored on foot – most shops are concentrated within a 10-minute walking radius.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Kamakura (approximately 1 hour from Tokyo by JR Yokosuka Line from Tokyo Station, ~¥940 each way). Visit the iconic Great Buddha (Kotoku-in Daibutsu, ¥300) – a 13.35-meter bronze Buddha statue dating from 1252. Explore the surrounding Kotoku-in temple grounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Kamakura. Visit Tsurugaoka Hachimangu Shrine, Kamakura's most important shrine, and stroll along Komachi-dori shopping street for local snacks and crafts. Hike the Daibutsu Hiking Trail through forested hills connecting multiple temples for scenic views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo by 18:00–19:00. Enjoy a final evening in Roppongi – visit Mori Art Museum (¥2,000) on the 53rd floor of Mori Tower for contemporary art and the Tokyo City View observation deck. The evening skyline from here is spectacular.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departing
meals.lunch: Kamakura – Nakamura-an, a traditional soba restaurant near Tsurugaoka Hachimangu serving handmade soba noodles (~¥1,500–¥2,500). Try the shirasu (whitebait) rice bowl, a Kamakura specialty.
meals.dinner: Roppongi – Gonpachi Nishi-Azabu (the restaurant that inspired the Kill Bill fight scene) for robata grilled skewers and sake in a dramatic multi-floor setting (~¥3,000–¥5,000)

day_by_day.notes: Kamakura is very popular on weekends – arrive early. The JR Pass covers the Yokosuka Line to Kamakura. The Daibutsu hiking trail is moderately challenging – wear proper footwear. Mori Art Museum tickets include the observation deck; book online to save time.

day_by_day.morning: Spend the morning in Shimokitazawa for a relaxed, local Sunday experience. Browse the weekend flea market at Shimokitazawa Station area, explore vintage clothing shops (the neighborhood has Tokyo's best vintage scene), and enjoy a leisurely brunch at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Daikanyama and Nakameguro – two of Tokyo's most stylish neighborhoods. Browse the Daikanyama T-Site (a beautiful bookstore complex in a forest-like setting) and explore boutiques. Walk along the Meguro River (lined with cherry trees – beautiful in April even post-blossom) to Nakameguro's trendy café and restaurant scene.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner in Tokyo. Head to Ebisu or Daikanyama for a memorable meal. Consider a teppanyaki or kaiseki (traditional Japanese multi-course) restaurant for a special farewell dinner experience.

meals.breakfast: Shimokitazawa – a local kissaten (retro coffee shop) for morning coffee, toast with butter and jam, and a boiled egg – the classic Japanese morning set (~¥600–¥1,000)
meals.lunch: Daikanyama – Ivy Place, a garden-terrace café-restaurant in the T-Site complex, serving brunch and light meals in a beautiful setting (~¥2,000–¥3,500)
meals.dinner: Ebisu – Tableaux for an upscale but mid-range kaiseki-influenced dinner, or Ebisu Yokocho (a covered alley of small restaurants) for a final izakaya crawl (~¥3,000–¥6,000)

day_by_day.notes: The Meguro River cherry blossoms typically peak in late March to early April – by April 26, you may see late blossoms or fresh green leaves, which are also beautiful. Daikanyama T-Site is open daily and is a must-visit for book lovers and design enthusiasts.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Spend time doing any last-minute souvenir shopping. Head to Asakusa's Nakamise-dori for traditional Japanese souvenirs (tenugui towels, kokeshi dolls, sensu fans), or visit a depachika (department store basement food hall) at Isetan Shinjuku or Mitsukoshi Ginza for premium Japanese food gifts: wagashi (traditional sweets), premium tea, sake, and packaged ramen.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the airport. Allow ample time: 2.5–3 hours before international departure. Take the Narita Express (N'EX) from Shinjuku (~¥3,070, ~80 minutes) or Airport Limousine Bus (~¥3,200, ~90–120 minutes depending on traffic). Check in, clear security, and browse the airport's excellent duty-free shops for last-minute Japanese whisky, Kit Kats, and cosmetics.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Tokyo.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast – enjoy a final Japanese breakfast with miso soup, rice, grilled fish, and pickles
meals.lunch: Airport – Narita International Airport has excellent dining options including ramen, sushi, and tempura restaurants in the departure terminal. Try Ippudo Ramen or a sushi conveyor belt restaurant (~¥1,500–¥2,500)
meals.dinner: On the plane

day_by_day.notes: Check your flight departure time and work backwards for airport arrival. For Narita Airport, allow at least 3 hours; for Haneda, 2.5 hours is usually sufficient. Return your Suica/Pasmo card at the airport for a refund of the ¥500 deposit (minus a small handling fee). Double-check hotel checkout time and arrange luggage storage if needed for the final morning of sightseeing.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Tokyo, Japan Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour
experiences.description: Explore the famous Tsukiji Outer Market, sampling fresh sushi, tamagoyaki, and street food from local vendors. Engage with fishmongers and food stall owners to learn about Tokyo's culinary heritage and the art of Japanese breakfast culture.

experiences.name: Akihabara Tech & Anime District Exploration
experiences.description: Dive deep into Tokyo's legendary electronics and tech culture hub. Visit multi-floor electronics stores like Yodobashi Camera, explore retro gaming arcades, maid cafes, and cutting-edge gadget shops that define Japan's unique intersection of technology and pop culture.

experiences.name: teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in a world-renowned digital art experience created by the art collective teamLab. Walk through stunning interactive installations that blend technology, nature, and art in a borderless, ever-changing environment — a perfect fusion of tech culture and artistic expression.

experiences.name: Senso-ji Temple & Asakusa Cultural Walk
experiences.description: Visit Tokyo's oldest and most iconic Buddhist temple, Senso-ji, and stroll through the historic Nakamise shopping street. Experience traditional ceremonies, purchase handcrafted souvenirs, and explore the preserved Edo-period atmosphere of Asakusa, one of Tokyo's most culturally rich neighborhoods.

experiences.name: Ramen Tasting Tour in Shinjuku
experiences.description: Embark on a self-guided or guided ramen crawl through Shinjuku's famous Ramen Street and surrounding alleyways. Sample regional ramen styles including tonkotsu, shoyu, and miso from legendary local ramen shops, and discover the craft and passion behind Japan's most beloved comfort food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival day — no morning activities scheduled. Flight UA arrives at 22:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival day — no afternoon activities scheduled.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at Narita/Haneda Airport at 22:30. Clear customs and immigration, then arrange a pre-booked luxury airport transfer (limousine service or private car) to Aegean Bliss Resort. Check in, unwind with a welcome amenity, and enjoy a late-night snack from the hotel's 24-hour room service menu — request a curated Japanese midnight snack platter with sake or premium green tea.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight
meals.lunch: N/A — in-flight
meals.dinner: Late-night room service at Aegean Bliss Resort: Japanese midnight snack platter (onigiri, edamame, miso soup) paired with premium Dassai 23 sake or ceremonial matcha

day_by_day.notes: Pre-arrange your luxury airport transfer before departure. Keep the first evening light — jet lag will be significant on arrival. Confirm hotel concierge services for the next 13 days upon check-in. Tokyo is in JST (UTC+9).

day_by_day.morning: Sleep in and recover from jet lag. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast at the resort's signature restaurant. After breakfast, take a gentle orientation stroll around your hotel neighborhood to acclimate to Tokyo's energy, sights, and sounds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the teamLab Borderless Digital Art Museum — a world-class immersive digital art experience featuring borderless rooms where art flows freely between spaces. Book a premium timed-entry slot in advance. Spend 2–3 hours wandering through luminous, interactive installations that blend technology and art seamlessly — perfect for easing into Tokyo's tech culture.
day_by_day.evening: Dine at a premium Kaiseki restaurant in the Odaiba or Minato area for an exquisite multi-course traditional Japanese dinner. Return to the hotel early to rest and prepare for the full days ahead.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort breakfast buffet featuring Japanese and Western options — fresh sashimi, tamagoyaki, miso soup, artisan pastries, and freshly brewed Kyoto-style drip coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at teamLab Borderless café — seasonal Japanese bento sets and matcha desserts in a stunning artistic environment
meals.dinner: Kaiseki dinner at Ryugin (Roppongi) or Ishikawa — expect 10+ course seasonal tasting menus with wine or sake pairing (reserve well in advance)

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Borderless requires advance booking — confirm tickets via the official website. Wear comfortable shoes as you'll be walking through large immersive spaces. This is a gentle day to ease into the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early for the Tsukiji Outer Market Food Tour. Arrive by 8:00 AM to experience the market at its freshest. Sample iconic street foods including ultra-fresh nigiri sushi, thick rolled tamagoyaki, grilled scallops, and tuna sashimi. Join a premium guided tour for insider access to the best stalls and hidden vendors.
day_by_day.afternoon: After the market, make your way to the nearby Hamarikyu Gardens — a stunning traditional Japanese garden set against the Tokyo skyline. Enjoy a matcha tea ceremony at the authentic teahouse on the central island. Afterward, explore the Ginza district for world-class luxury shopping at flagship stores including Hermès, Louis Vuitton, and Comme des Garçons.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten (Ginza) or Sushi Yoshitake — a legendary sushi omakase experience. Watch master chefs craft each piece with decades of precision. Pair with premium sake or champagne.

meals.breakfast: Tsukiji Outer Market — fresh tuna sashimi, grilled tamagoyaki skewers, sea urchin on rice, and freshly brewed canned coffee from local vendors
meals.lunch: Ginza Six rooftop restaurant or Kyubey Ginza — premium sushi lunch set with seasonal ingredients
meals.dinner: Omakase sushi at Sukiyabashi Jiro Honten or Sushi Yoshitake (Michelin 3-star) — 20-piece nigiri omakase with sake pairing (¥40,000–¥60,000 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Tsukiji Outer Market is open from approximately 5:00 AM. Arriving by 7:30–8:00 AM ensures the freshest products. Sushi omakase restaurants require reservations months in advance — book through your hotel concierge immediately. Dress smartly for Ginza and the evening restaurant.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to the Akihabara Tech & Anime District. Explore multi-floor electronics megastores like Yodobashi Camera and BIC Camera. Discover the latest gadgets, robotics, gaming hardware, and rare tech collectibles. Visit Akihabara's iconic maid cafés for a cultural experience, and browse specialty anime and manga shops.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Akihabara's hidden gems — visit Super Potato for retro gaming nostalgia, explore Radio Kaikan for premium figurines and collectibles, and stop at the Gundam Café for a uniquely Japanese pop-culture experience. Then head to the nearby Ochanomizu area to visit the MIDI instrument stores and music tech shops.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shinjuku for the evening. Visit the observation deck of the Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building for free panoramic night views of the city. Then dine in the vibrant Shinjuku Kabukicho district.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast at Aegean Bliss Resort — Japanese set with grilled fish, rice, miso soup, and pickles
meals.lunch: Akihabara — premium ramen at Fuunji (tsukemen-style) or a traditional tonkatsu lunch at Maisen Akihabara
meals.dinner: Shinjuku — Narisawa or Kozue (Park Hyatt Tokyo, 40th floor) for contemporary Japanese cuisine with sweeping city views

day_by_day.notes: Akihabara is best explored on foot — wear comfortable shoes. The area is most vibrant from 11:00 AM onwards. Kozue at Park Hyatt requires reservations — book through your hotel concierge. This is the hotel from the film 'Lost in Translation,' adding a cultural layer to the dining experience.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Senso-ji Temple in Asakusa — Tokyo's oldest and most revered Buddhist temple. Arrive early (before 8:00 AM) to experience the temple in tranquility before crowds arrive. Walk through the iconic Kaminarimon Gate, stroll along Nakamise-dori shopping street, and draw an omikuji (fortune) at the temple.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the surrounding Asakusa neighborhood — browse the Kappabashi 'Kitchen Town' street for premium Japanese kitchenware, lacquerware, and handcrafted knives. Visit the Asakusa Culture Tourist Information Center rooftop for panoramic views of Senso-ji and the Tokyo Skytree. Take a traditional rickshaw (jinrikisha) ride through old Asakusa streets.
day_by_day.evening: Ascend Tokyo Skytree — the world's tallest broadcasting tower — for spectacular 360-degree views from the Tembo Deck (350m) and Tembo Galleria (450m). Book a premium sunset slot for golden hour views. Dine at one of the Skytree Town restaurants afterward.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at Asakusa — Asakusa Imahan for traditional Japanese breakfast or Pelican Café for artisan toast and coffee
meals.lunch: Asakusa Mugitoro — premium tororo (mountain yam) cuisine in a beautiful traditional setting near Senso-ji
meals.dinner: Skytree Town — Wa Yamamura or Sky Restaurant 634 for Japanese fine dining with panoramic Tokyo night views

day_by_day.notes: Senso-ji is open 24/7 but the inner hall opens at 6:00 AM. Arriving at 7:00–8:00 AM provides the best atmosphere. Book Tokyo Skytree fast-track tickets in advance to avoid queues. April in Tokyo may mean cherry blossom season — check Ueno Park (nearby) for possible hanami opportunities.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the upscale Omotesando and Harajuku neighborhoods. Walk the iconic Omotesando Boulevard — Tokyo's answer to the Champs-Élysées — lined with flagship architecture by world-renowned designers (Prada by Herzog & de Meuron, Tod's by Toyo Ito). Visit Omotesando Hills for luxury shopping. Explore the hidden backstreets of Ura-Harajuku for independent designer boutiques.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Nezu Museum — a world-class private museum housing an exquisite collection of pre-modern Asian art set within a stunning bamboo garden. Afterward, explore the Aoyama district for contemporary art galleries and design studios. Visit the Watari-um Museum of Contemporary Art for cutting-edge exhibitions.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Shibuya for the evening. Experience the world-famous Shibuya Scramble Crossing — best viewed from the Mag's Park rooftop or Starbucks Reserve Roastery Shibuya. Dine in the Daikanyama or Nakameguro area for a more intimate, upscale evening.

meals.breakfast: Omotesando — Bread, Espresso & (Cafe Epi) for premium French-Japanese fusion breakfast, or bills Omotesando for ricotta hotcakes
meals.lunch: Omotesando Hills — Tableaux or a premium bento from Isetan's basement food hall (depachika)
meals.dinner: Nakameguro — Craftale or Florilège for innovative French-Japanese cuisine along the scenic canal (Michelin-starred)

day_by_day.notes: The Nezu Museum garden is particularly beautiful in spring — azaleas typically bloom in April. Book Florilège well in advance as it's one of Tokyo's most sought-after reservations. The Shibuya Scramble is most dramatic at night when neon lights illuminate the crossing.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Nikko or Hakone (choose based on weather and preference). Recommended: Hakone for a luxury onsen (hot spring) experience with views of Mt. Fuji. Take the Romancecar limited express train from Shinjuku Station. Upon arrival, visit the Hakone Open Air Museum — a spectacular outdoor sculpture park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Hakone — ride the Hakone Ropeway over volcanic Owakudani Valley for dramatic views. Take a cruise on Lake Ashi with potential Mt. Fuji views on clear days. Visit the Hakone Shrine torii gate rising from the lake for iconic photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Check into a premium ryokan (traditional inn) in Hakone for an overnight stay, or return to Tokyo by evening. If staying: enjoy a kaiseki dinner at your ryokan followed by a private onsen bath. If returning: light dinner at the hotel or a soba restaurant near Shinjuku Station.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before departure, or purchase an ekiben (premium station bento) at Shinjuku Station for the train journey
meals.lunch: Hakone — Naraya Café near Miyanoshita Station for seasonal Japanese lunch with mountain views, or restaurant at the Hakone Open Air Museum
meals.dinner: Hakone Ryokan kaiseki dinner (if staying overnight) at Gora Kadan or Hakone Ginyu — 10-course seasonal menu with local Hakone ingredients and sake pairing

day_by_day.notes: Mt. Fuji visibility depends heavily on weather and season — April can be clear but clouds are common in the afternoon. Book Gora Kadan or similar premium ryokan months in advance. The Hakone Free Pass covers most transportation within Hakone. If returning to Tokyo, last Romancecar trains depart Hakone-Yumoto around 9:00 PM.

day_by_day.morning: Return to Tokyo if overnight in Hakone, or begin the day fresh from the hotel. Visit the Mori Art Museum in Roppongi Hills — one of Tokyo's premier contemporary art spaces located on the 53rd floor with sweeping city views. The adjacent Tokyo City View observation deck offers 360-degree panoramas.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Roppongi Art Triangle — visit the National Art Center Tokyo (largest exhibition space in Japan) and 21_21 Design Sight in Midtown Tokyo, designed by Tadao Ando. Browse the Midtown Galleria for luxury shopping and design goods. This afternoon is a deep dive into Tokyo's world-class contemporary art and design culture.
day_by_day.evening: Ramen Tasting Tour in Shinjuku — embark on a premium guided ramen crawl through Shinjuku's legendary Ramen Street and surrounding alleys. Sample different regional styles: rich tonkotsu from Hakata, complex shoyu from Tokyo, and creamy miso from Sapporo. Pair with craft Japanese beer or highballs.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or Roppongi Hills — Café Keyaki for a refined Japanese-Western breakfast
meals.lunch: National Art Center Tokyo — Brasserie Paul Bocuse Le Musée — an elegant French brasserie inside the museum itself, offering a premium lunch set
meals.dinner: Shinjuku Ramen Tour — Fuunji (tsukemen), Ichiran (solo booth tonkotsu), and Nagi (niboshi/sardine broth) — budget ¥3,000–¥5,000 per person for the full crawl experience

day_by_day.notes: The Mori Art Museum is open until 10:00 PM on most days, making it flexible for scheduling. The ramen crawl is best done with a guide — book through a reputable tour operator like Airbnb Experiences or Govoyagin. Pace yourself — ramen portions are filling.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Imperial Palace East Gardens — the former site of Edo Castle's innermost circles, now a serene public garden in the heart of Tokyo. Walk through the Ninomaru Garden and enjoy the seasonal flora. Nearby, visit the National Museum of Modern Art (MOMAT) for an outstanding collection of 20th-century Japanese art.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Akihabara for a second, deeper tech exploration — this time focusing on Japan's robotics and AI culture. Visit the Digital Hollywood University Gallery or explore the latest consumer robotics at specialized stores. Then visit the nearby Kanda Myojin Shrine — uniquely, this shrine blesses IT companies and technology, a fascinating intersection of ancient culture and modern tech.
day_by_day.evening: Experience a traditional Japanese performance — book tickets for a Kabuki performance at Kabukiza Theatre in Ginza (one of the world's most spectacular theatrical buildings). Single-act tickets are available for those new to Kabuki. Dress elegantly for the evening.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — request a traditional Japanese set: grilled salmon, rice, miso soup, pickled vegetables, and green tea
meals.lunch: Marunouchi area — Michelin-starred Quintessence or a premium lunch at the Palace Hotel Tokyo's Crown restaurant overlooking the Imperial Palace moat
meals.dinner: Post-Kabuki dinner in Ginza — Ginza Kojyu (Michelin 3-star) for exquisite kaiseki, or Beige Alain Ducasse Tokyo in the Chanel building for Franco-Japanese haute cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Imperial Palace East Gardens are closed on Mondays and Fridays — verify the schedule. Kabukiza Theatre single-act tickets (hitomakumi) can be purchased on the day but availability is limited — book in advance through the official website. Earphone guides with English commentary are available.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Yanaka district — one of Tokyo's most beautifully preserved historic neighborhoods that survived WWII bombing. Wander through Yanaka Cemetery (famous for cherry blossom trees), explore the narrow Yanaka Ginza shopping street, and visit independent artisan shops, galleries, and traditional craft studios. This is old Tokyo at its most authentic.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ueno for the Tokyo National Museum — Japan's oldest and largest museum housing the world's greatest collection of Japanese art and artifacts, including samurai armor, ancient ceramics, Buddhist sculptures, and ukiyo-e woodblock prints. Spend 2–3 hours in the Honkan (Japanese Gallery) and Heiseikan buildings.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the teamLab Planets in Toyosu (different from Borderless) — an immersive water-themed digital art installation where you walk through knee-deep water surrounded by infinite reflections. Book a premium evening slot for a magical experience. Afterward, explore the Toyosu area's waterfront.

meals.breakfast: Yanaka — Kayaba Coffee, a beloved retro kissaten (coffee shop) dating to 1938, serving morning sets with thick toast, egg, and drip coffee
meals.lunch: Ueno — Ueno Seiyoken, a historic French restaurant established in 1872 serving elegant Western-Japanese fusion cuisine in a grand setting
meals.dinner: Toyosu — Sushi Saito (if reservation available) or Tsukiji Sushiko Honten for premium fresh seafood, followed by craft cocktails at a Toyosu waterfront bar

day_by_day.notes: teamLab Planets requires advance booking and sells out weeks ahead — confirm tickets early. You will walk barefoot through water installations — leave valuables and electronics secured. The Yanaka district is best explored in the morning when local life is most active.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to Kyoto via Shinkansen (bullet train) — approximately 2 hours 15 minutes from Tokyo Station on the Nozomi. Visit the iconic Fushimi Inari Shrine with its thousands of vermilion torii gates winding up the mountain. Hike the lower trails for dramatic photography and spiritual atmosphere.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the Gion district — Kyoto's famous geisha quarter. Walk the cobblestone Hanamikoji Street, lined with traditional machiya townhouses and exclusive ochaya (teahouses). Visit Kennin-ji Temple (Kyoto's oldest Zen temple) and the stunning Nishiki Market — Kyoto's 'Kitchen' with over 100 specialty food stalls.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Tokyo via Shinkansen (last Nozomi trains depart Kyoto around 9:00 PM). Alternatively, if budget allows, book a premium room at Aman Kyoto or The Ritz-Carlton Kyoto for one night to fully savor the city. Return to Tokyo the following morning.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast before early departure, or Shinkansen ekiben — purchase a premium Kyoto-style bento at Tokyo Station's Gransta food hall
meals.lunch: Kyoto — Kikunoi Honten for Kyoto kaiseki cuisine (Michelin 2-star) — book in advance
meals.dinner: Kyoto — Mizai or Nakamura (one of Japan's oldest restaurants, established 1716) for an unforgettable Kyoto kaiseki dinner, or return to Tokyo for a light dinner at the hotel

day_by_day.notes: Book Shinkansen tickets in advance through JR Pass or Smartex. The first Nozomi from Tokyo departs around 6:00 AM — aim to arrive in Kyoto by 8:30 AM for maximum time. Fushimi Inari is most atmospheric at sunrise or late afternoon when crowds thin. Gion has strict photography etiquette — do not photograph geiko or maiko without permission.

day_by_day.morning: Dedicate the morning to a premium Japanese cooking class — learn to prepare authentic dishes including dashi broth, miso soup, tamagoyaki, and sushi rolls under the guidance of a professional Japanese chef. Classes are available through providers like Cooking Sun or WAFU Japanese Cooking in Tokyo, offering intimate small-group or private sessions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sony ExploraScience or the Miraikan (National Museum of Emerging Science and Innovation) on Odaiba Island — a world-class science and technology museum featuring ASIMO robot demonstrations, interactive AI exhibits, a 360-degree digital Earth display, and cutting-edge innovation showcases. This is Tokyo's tech culture at its most inspiring.
day_by_day.evening: Final luxury shopping evening — visit Isetan Shinjuku (Japan's most prestigious department store) for premium Japanese goods, fashion, and the legendary basement depachika food hall. Purchase premium gifts: wagyu beef, Kyoto sweets, sake, and artisan crafts. End the evening with a cocktail at the New York Bar, Park Hyatt Tokyo (52nd floor).

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — final full Japanese breakfast: grilled fish, rice, miso soup, pickles, natto, and green tea
meals.lunch: Post-cooking class — enjoy the dishes you prepared with your chef instructor, paired with Japanese green tea and sake
meals.dinner: Shinjuku — Tempura Kondo (Michelin 2-star) for the finest tempura in Tokyo, where seasonal vegetables and seafood are elevated to an art form, followed by cocktails at New York Bar (Park Hyatt)

day_by_day.notes: Book the cooking class at least 1 week in advance — private sessions are available for premium experiences. Miraikan ASIMO demonstrations are scheduled at specific times — check the website for the current schedule. The New York Bar has a cover charge on evenings with live music — this is highly recommended for a cinematic Tokyo farewell.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Tokyo. Enjoy a leisurely hotel breakfast and begin packing. Take one last stroll through your neighborhood to soak in Tokyo's atmosphere — visit a local convenience store (konbini) for last-minute snacks and gifts, and pick up premium Japanese whisky or sake from a nearby liquor specialist.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on your departure flight time: visit the Shibuya Sky observation deck (atop Shibuya Scramble Square) for final panoramic views of the city, or revisit a favorite neighborhood for a last walk. Check out of the hotel and arrange your luxury private transfer to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Depart Tokyo. Arrive at the airport 3 hours before international departure. Enjoy the premium airport lounges (JAL Sakura Lounge or ANA Suite Lounge at Haneda, or the IASS Executive Lounge at Narita) for a final taste of Japanese hospitality before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Aegean Bliss Resort — final hotel breakfast, savoring every last dish
meals.lunch: Airport or neighborhood farewell meal — Tonkatsu Maisen near Omotesando for a quintessential Japanese tonkatsu set, or a premium soba lunch at Honmura An
meals.dinner: Airport premium lounge dining or in-flight (request a Japanese meal option when booking your flight)

day_by_day.notes: Allow ample time for airport transit — Tokyo's airports are large and international security can take 45–60 minutes. Liquids purchased at duty-free must comply with airline regulations. Consider shipping excess luggage home via Japan Post's Takkyubin service — reliable, affordable, and available from most hotels. Sayonara, Tokyo!
